transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what finally made me come in is I keep having this feeling that I’ve ruined things for everybody. Like, not just made a normal mistake, but like I’m the reason things are harder for people around me.

I’m in an apprenticeship, and I keep feeling like I’m kind of a fake there, like I don’t really belong and everyone’s going to realize it. And when something goes wrong, even stuff that other people would probably just fix and move on from, I get stuck on it. I think about how I let my family down, and even the younger apprentices, like I’m supposed to be someone they can look to a little bit, and instead I feel like I’m just messing things up for everyone. It’s been weighing on me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once found pleasurable now feel like a chore?

Yeah… I have noticed that. It’s kind of one of the things that made me feel like something was really off, because it’s not just being busy or tired.

Like, I used to draw a lot — I’d keep my sketchbook nearby and even if I only had a little time, I’d want to add something to it. Now I can walk right past it for days and it’s like… nothing. I don’t even feel guilty in the normal way, just kind of blank about it. And volleyball used to be this thing that helped me feel like myself, like I could just show up and move around and not think so much. Lately I skip it, and when I think about going it feels like another task I have to force myself through.

Same with the volunteer group I’m in. I used to actually like getting the texts and figuring out when I could help, but now I see the messages come in and I just ignore them. Not because I stopped caring exactly, but because I don’t feel that pull toward it anymore. It’s like the things that used to make me feel like me are still sitting there, but I can’t really reach the feeling I’m supposed to have about them.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or like you’re a burden to others, even when things aren’t really your fault?

Yeah… yes. That’s honestly probably the main thing that pushed me to make the appointment.

I keep getting this feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody, even when, if I try to look at it logically, I know it’s probably not that dramatic. Like in the apprenticeship, if something goes wrong or I don’t understand something as fast as I think I should, I don’t just think, “Okay, I’m learning.” I start feeling like I’m a fake, like I somehow slipped in and everyone’s going to figure out I don’t belong there.

And then it spreads out in my head. It’s not just about the job — I start thinking I’m letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices, which sounds maybe kind of weird, but I feel like I’m supposed to be someone they can at least trust or look to a little bit. And instead I’m sitting there thinking I’m making things harder for everyone or disappointing people.

The frustrating part is that some of the stuff I get stuck on is stuff I know other people would probably just fix and move on from. Like they’d say, “Okay, that happened, let’s correct it.” But I carry it around like it proves something bad about me. So yeah… I do feel guilty, and like a burden, even when part of me knows it isn’t really all my fault.
Do you find yourself feeling like you’re completely worthless or that you deserve to be punished for things you’ve done, even when others wouldn’t see them as that serious?

Yeah… I mean, “deserve to be punished” sounds really intense, and I don’t know if I’d say it exactly like that, but I do get this feeling like I’ve done something wrong enough that I don’t really deserve people’s patience with me.

It’s like, what made me come in is that I keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody. In the apprenticeship, if I mess something up or don’t catch on quickly, I don’t just see it as a mistake someone can fix. I start thinking, “Okay, this proves I’m a fake. I don’t actually belong here. Everyone’s going to realize they made a mistake letting me be here.”

And then I start thinking about my family, like I’m letting them down after they expected me to do something with myself. And even the younger apprentices — which I know maybe sounds like I’m putting too much on myself — but I feel like I’m supposed to be someone they can count on a little, or at least not someone making things harder. So when something goes wrong, even small stuff that other people would probably just correct and move on from, I carry it around like it means I’m worthless or like I’ve disappointed everyone.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Yeah… more the moving slowly part, I think. I don’t feel like I’m bouncing off the walls or anything. It’s more like my body has this drag to it.

At work especially, I catch myself doing things slower than I normally would. Like something simple — climbing down to grab or check a fitting, or turning around to answer the foreman when he asks me something — it feels like it takes this extra push, like I have to talk myself into each step. And I know that probably sounds minor, but in that kind of job you can really tell when you’re not moving like yourself, because everything is so physical and there’s always someone waiting on something.

A couple people have asked me if I’m sick, or if I’m hungover, which was embarrassing because I’m not trying to look out of it. I’ll be standing there thinking I’m acting normal, and then someone says that, and I realize I must seem slowed down from the outside too. It’s not every single second, but yeah… enough that other people have noticed.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, guilty, and lost interest in things, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I think this is the longest it’s been, honestly. It’s not like it just started last week or something. I’d say this stretch has been going on for about nine months, give or take.

At first I sort of told myself it was just stress or that I was tired and needed to get organized, because it wasn’t immediately obvious to everyone else. I could still kind of push through and make myself show up, so I kept thinking, “Okay, maybe this is just a rough patch.” But it stayed. It didn’t really lift the way I kept expecting it to.

It became a lot harder to hide once school and work started slipping, though. That’s when I couldn’t just explain it away in my head anymore, because it was actually showing up in things I was supposed to be handling. Before that I think I was covering it better, or at least trying to. But yeah… this has been with me for months. Around nine months.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, or felt guilty for at least two weeks straight?

I’m honestly not sure. I mean, I’ve had times before where I felt low or kind of disappointed in myself, like anyone does, especially when things were stressful, but I don’t know if I can point to another clear stretch before this where it was two weeks straight and really like this.

I keep trying to think back and separate “I was having a bad couple days” from “I was actually stuck in it,” if that makes sense. There were definitely times I got down on myself, but I don’t remember it lasting in the same steady way or taking over the way this current period has. So… I don’t think I can say yes for sure. This is the first time I’ve really recognized it as something that didn’t just pass.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, or felt guilty for at least two weeks straight without improvement?

I don’t think I can say that I have, not in a clear way. Like, I’ve definitely had rough patches before where I felt down or kind of guilty about not doing enough, but I don’t remember a time before this where it was two weeks straight with no improvement and I could point to it like, “Yeah, that was the same thing.”

I might’ve had bad days strung together here and there, but they’d usually break up, or something would distract me, or I’d feel more like myself again for a bit. This current stretch is the one that feels different because it didn’t really let up. So I guess my answer is… not that I know of.
Have you ever had a period in the past, before this current one, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or felt guilty most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I don’t really think so, no—not in the way you’re describing it, like most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight.

I’ve been trying to go back through it in my head, because I don’t want to just say no if I’m forgetting something, but before this current stretch, I mostly remember shorter periods where I’d feel bad about myself or get kind of low for a few days. Or I’d have a rough week, maybe, depending on what was going on. But it didn’t feel like this steady thing that just sat on top of me all day every day.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’m not aware of any past period like that. This is the first one I can really identify as lasting and not improving.
